title: Inattentional Blindness
summary: A demanding count on a dense static display that also contains an object nobody mentioned, followed by a recognition question and the same display again with everything marked. The demonstration works once, and the page is built so that nothing before the task gives it away.
learningObjectives: Experience directly that a demanding task can leave a fully visible object unreported.
Distinguish attention from awareness, and say why the two are not the same thing.
Explain why not reporting an object is not the same as not seeing it.
Recognise that the outcome is a property of the display and the task rather than of the observer.
Say why a demonstration of this kind cannot be repeated on the same person.
interactionTypes: commitment to a counting task before any hint of the critical object
performed count on a dense static display
recognition question that is reported rather than scored
transparent replay of the same display with everything marked
two deterministic display variants handed out in order
demonstrator route that reveals the design and says it spends the screen
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. The count and the recognition answer stay in the page and are gone when it is closed. Which display variants have been used is a JavaScript variable that a reload forgets.
accessibilityNotes: The display is static: nothing moves, flashes or changes, and there is no time limit on the count, so there is nothing for a reduced-motion setting to switch off. Shape and fill carry the task and colour never does; every item is drawn in one colour. The display carries a description that states what is on it and what to count, written so that it does not give away the demonstration. The replay afterwards carries its own description naming everything that is marked. Keyboard operable throughout, and the count accepts Enter. The recognition question is a report with no correct answer and nothing is marked right or wrong.
dataStatus: Generated. Every display is produced in the browser from a fixed seed, so a given variant is identical on every machine. No real stimulus set, image or participant data is used, and the activity reports no noticing rates because this collection has none.
simulationNotes: Displays are laid out on a 12 by 7 grid with per-item jitter from a seeded generator. The counted type, solid down-pointing triangles, is forced to between six and ten instances so the count is never trivially small; no other item is a solid down-pointing triangle. The unasked-for object is a five-pointed outlined star placed in a free cell away from the middle, because an object at the point of fixation would be a different demonstration. Variant A uses 48 items and variant B uses 72; they are handed out in order and the tool refuses a third run in one session.
readmeTopic: attention, awareness, and an object in plain view that goes unreported
